newsitem.title: NORWAY: ONE-OFF COSTS BURDEN UBN H1 PROFITS.
newsitem.headline: ONE-OFF COSTS BURDEN UBN H1 PROFITS.

text.p: Union Bank of Norway, the country's biggest savings bank, on Thursday said lower capital gains and one-off costs burdened first-half 1997 profits.
The bank said the operating profit before losses and writedowns fell to 652 million crowns from 666 million in the corresponding 1996 period.
The operating profit dropped to 581 million from 761 million and the net profit was trimmed to 417 million from 559 million.
"Operating profit of 652 million crowns before losses and write-downs during the first half-year is very good and on the same level as last year," President and CEO Kjell O. Kran said in a statement.

"The slightly weaker operating result after losses (581 million) than in 1996 is primarily a result of UBN's write-down of 93 million crowns on its purchase of 10 percent of the shares in Fokus Bank, and of the Board's allocation of 30 million crowns to an employees' fund in connection with the bank's 175 years' anniversary in May. The bank has also seen lower capital gains this year," he said.

Net interest income rose to 1.25 billion crowns from 1.24 billion while non-interest operating income grew to 905 million from 778 million. In the second quarter, the average customer margin has been 2.8 percent, the bank said.
"We are satisfied with the results and expect that 1997 will be another good year for Union Bank of Norway,' Kran said.
But the price of UBN primary capital certificate, a hybrid share, fell three crowns to 241 crowns in afternoon trade on the Oslo Bourse.

Kran emphasised that the share acquisition in Fokus Bank was a pre-condition for the development of a close long-term business partnership between UBN and Fokus, Norway's third largest commercial bank.
The development of this partnership will be one of the bank's most important tasks in the future, he said.
"The goal of the partnership is that both banks will be able to offer the market more competitive financial services and products, thereby improving the banks' profitability," Kran said.
UBN and Fokus expect to conclude talks on a comprehensive cooperation package by the end of August, the bank said.

UBN and Fokus announced on May 7 they had started talks to establish cooperation based on both banks continuing as independent entities. They also launched a joint cooperation in insurance with Danish insurer Codan Forsikring.

UBN and Codan, which has a separate cooperation with Fokus, are in negotiations on insurance operations in Norway. It is expected that Codan will take over as the major shareholder in NOR Forsikring in the near future, UBN said.
UBN, known locally as Sparebanken NOR, also has cooperation agreements with five regional savings banks.

"Fokus Bank, UBN and our five partner savings banks will have indisputably the best distribution system for financial services, with a total of 427 branches covering all of Norway's counties," Kran said.
UBN's total assets have grown 19 percent over the past twelve months. The increased activity has increased the revenue for the Group, particularly for its subsidiaries.
More business also led to increased costs, with operating costs growing to 1.50 billion crowns from 1.35 billion.
"The cost growth is higher than it would have been with a lower growth rate," Kran said. "Our measures to reduce the bank's costs are, however, being closely monitored."
--Rolf Soderlind, Oslo newsroom +47 22 42 50 41
